item.title: Russian, Ukrainian delegations arrive in Abu Dhabi for talks -- sources
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
ABU DHABI, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- Russian and Ukrainian delegations arrived in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), on Monday to participate in trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, informed sources confirmed to Xinhua. The talks are scheduled to take place on Tuesday and Wednesday as part of ongoing efforts to explore ways to resolve the Ukraine crisis. Earlier on Monday, Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, announced on Telegram that the Ukrainian negotiating team was heading to the UAE for the talks. Representatives of European countries, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Italy, as well as officials from NATO and the European Commission, will also be present in Abu Dhabi, he said. Umerov added that Ukraine plans to hold separate coordination meetings with its European partners. "Our goal is a long-term and sustainable peace, guaranteed security for Ukraine, and real opportunities for Ukraine's post-war recovery," he said. The Abu Dhabi meeting will mark the first trilateral meeting between Russia, the United States and Ukraine since February.■

item.title: China's second homegrown large cruise ship starts first trial voyage
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
SHANGHAI, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, departed from the Shanghai Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal in east China on Monday, starting its first trial voyage. The ship is scheduled to arrive at the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou, south China, on Nov. 12. This voyage is set to comprehensively test the cruise ship's operational capabilities, marking a key step toward formal commercial operation. During the voyage, systematic tests and adjustments will be carried out in areas including maritime operations, navigation safety, products and services, ship-shore coordination, and ship-wide information systems, according to the operator. Under simulated real operating conditions, stress tests will also be conducted on core guest experiences such as cabin service, dining and entertainment, and shopping and leisure, to further examine coordination and response capabilities among various departments. A manager with Adora Cruises said the first trial voyage is an important part of preparations for the ship's maiden voyage, and serves as a real-world test of operational support capabilities, product experience and service procedures. After arriving in Guangzhou, the ship will proceed with preparations for home port berthing, port coordination and maiden voyage service procedures. A second trial voyage is planned for Nov. 14-16, and the ship will launch its inaugural season from Guangzhou on Nov. 22. ■

item.title: China's emerging, future industries achieve momentum via new blueprints
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- From intelligent connected new energy vehicles and biomanufacturing to quantum precision measurement, China is materializing its industrial ambitions with the guidance of a cluster of detailed five-year sector blueprints. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the country aims to speed up the development of strategic emerging industries while cultivating future industries as new growth drivers. These sector plans, together with national guidelines on new quality productive forces issued in October, provide a detailed framework for moving Chinese industry up the value chain. More than listing promising technologies, these plans identify how innovations will be led to production, and where new products can be applied. This is crucial to the next stage of China's high-quality development. ANCHORING FRONTIER TRACKS These sector-specific blueprints highlight sci-tech innovations, with advancing industrial modernization acting as the guiding principle. The five-year plan for electronic information manufacturing development issued in September clearly illustrates this approach. It calls for developing frontier electronic measurement technologies such as high-bandwidth, terahertz and quantum precision measurement. Motivated by this deployment, Ceyear Technologies Co., Ltd. has strengthened its technological research and launched a new generation of electronic measurement products, the performance of which, it says, matches advanced international standards. Its products, notably, already serve several strategic emerging industries like aerospace, satellite communications and AI. Similar priorities run through other plans, but with different industrial entry points. The plan for the pharmaceutical industry puts innovation first among eight major tasks, and identifies frontier technologies for basic research, technology transfer and industrial maturation. The plan for renewable energy development emphasizes frontier, original and disruptive technology research and equipment breakthroughs, while the green and low-carbon industry plan urges tackling key technologies for clean and low-carbon hydrogen, and speeding up the development and application of high-performance and degradable bio-based materials. These forward-looking measures could spark breakthroughs in frontier technologies needed to drive overall industrial upgrading, help China's industries move toward the middle and high ends of the global value chain, and strengthen their international competitiveness, said Deng Zhonghan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. BUILDING INDUSTRIALIZATION BRIDGES Selecting promising fields is only the first step. Hard-technology projects often require long investment cycles, while many research teams lack pilot facilities and first customers. The plans therefore seek to make companies central to innovation and connect research with industrial demand. Chinese enterprises already account for more than 75 percent of the country's total R&D spending for several consecutive years, making them the mainstay of sci-tech innovations. In Chongqing Municipality in southwest China, a biomanufacturing pilot platform offers a glimpse of such a bridge being built. Rows of reactors and purification equipment are undergoing process validation before production begins. Put into use in June 2026, this platform has signed up more than 20 research teams and enterprises, allowing them to test and refine processes without each having to build a full pilot line. "The pilot platform has addressed our urgent need in commercializing research results and significantly reduced R&D investment and trial costs," said Ou Zhen, director of the general manager's office at Hymos (Chongqing) Bioscience Co., Ltd., adding that the company has developed 17 types of recombinant human keratin and is advancing the commercialization of multiple keratin products with the platform's support. China's policy toolkit extends beyond shared facilities. Companies are encouraged to lead national science and technology tasks, while cross-sector innovation consortia can bring manufacturers, suppliers and researchers together. Universities and research institutes, meanwhile, are encouraged to license results to small and medium-sized enterprises on a "use first, pay later" basis. Talent and finance policies complete the support system, promoting closer industry-education integration and calling for more patient capital that invests early, in small companies, for the long term, and in hard technology. PROVIDING NEW OPPORTUNITIES The strategy is not confined to industries still in their infancy. The October guidelines specify support for upgrading traditional industries via digital, intelligent and green technologies, while identifying industries such as mining, metallurgy, chemicals, light industry, textiles, machinery, shipbuilding and construction. In a high-tech zone in Weifang, east China's Shandong Province, engines move along intelligent production lines at a Weichai Group workshop. From diesel engines to new energy, technological upgrade of this leading traditional power equipment maker illustrates how innovation can transform an established manufacturer, rather than simply replace old industries with new ones. This combination of new industries and modernized existing ones is key to the development of new quality productive forces. Frontier sectors can create fresh growth drivers, while a broader industrial base supplies components, engineering expertise and markets for their products. "The real test of new quality productive forces is not under the spotlight at a press conference, but in companies' actual financial statements," said Yan Yang, vice president of the Beijing Internet of Things Intelligent Technology Application Association. These plans also create potential entry points for international partners. The October guidelines call for a global innovation cooperation network, including joint science parks, Belt and Road joint laboratories, and international centers for applying advanced technologies. They encourage foreign venture-capital institutions and international standards organizations to develop in China, and call for efficient, convenient and secure cross-border data flows. Some foreign companies are already positioning themselves around the opportunities brought by China's emerging and future industries. Corning Incorporated is expanding optical-communications capacity in east China's Shanghai, and south China's Guangdong and Hainan, as the country's industrial digitalization increases demand for upstream materials. General Electric's energy investment arm in China, meanwhile, has joined China Huadian Corporation and Peking University's energy research institute in research on hydrogen applications. Such projects show how overseas technology, capital and expertise can connect with Chinese manufacturing, infrastructure and research capabilities. The guidelines urge local governments to adapt industries to local strengths, avoid blind investment and prevent "involution-style" competition. If these guardrails hold, the blueprints could turn a dispersed set of technology bets into a more coherent industrial pipeline, which will foster new growth engines, upgrade China's manufacturing foundation, and provide overseas partners with a clearer roadmap for initiating and advancing collaboration. ■

item.title: The world comes to China, opportunities flow both ways
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
* This year's China International Import Expo has brought together 162 countries, regions and international organizations, attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors and seen its total exhibition area exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time. * For many overseas exhibitors, the expo is more than a six-day event. The connections established at the expo can develop into lasting business relationships, while continued engagement with the Chinese market can open up new areas of cooperation. SHANGHAI, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- As tariffs rise, trade restrictions multiply and geopolitical tensions weigh on global economic ties, the case for keeping markets open has become increasingly urgent. Against this backdrop, the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which opened here on Thursday, sends a message that stands in contrast to the growing tide of protectionism: China is continuing to open its market wider and share development opportunities with the world. This year's expo has brought together 162 countries, regions and international organizations, attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors and seen its total exhibition area exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time. Behind these expanding figures are businesses of different sizes and from different parts of the world, bringing products, technologies and expertise to China while seeking new markets, partners and opportunities for cooperation. WIDER DOOR TO A VAST MARKET At a time when some economies are raising barriers to protect domestic industries, China's decision to continue hosting an import-focused expo on an ever-expanding scale carries particular significance. For overseas businesses, the CIIE offers a rare opportunity to meet Chinese importers, distributors, retailers and consumers in one place. Australian dairy producer Bulla, for instance, has returned to the CIIE every year since 2019. Its participation has helped it move from limited brand recognition in China to a growing network of business relationships in retail and food services. At the 2025 expo, the company reached a direct-sourcing agreement with Chinese grocery platform Dingdong Fresh. "It's progressing very well," Sam Zhang, who oversees international business at Bulla, said of the partnership. According to Zhang, the company's exports to China exceeded 10 million Australian dollars (6.9 million U.S. dollars) in the financial year ended June 2026. For other companies, the expo offers a chance to introduce new products and explore untapped opportunities in the Chinese market. Italian truffle producer Urbani Tartufi is attending the CIIE for the first time, seeking to introduce fresh truffles to Chinese consumers and explore the procedures for exports to China. The company already sells processed truffle products in the Chinese market but sees further potential in bringing its fresh produce to local consumers. "We have high expectations for the Chinese market and hope to establish closer business ties through the expo," said Olga Urbani, the company's president. Also making its CIIE debut is Colombia-based oil producer DAABON Group. Balachandar Selvamohan, the company's global innovation director, said company representatives had visited the previous two editions and saw the potential benefits of exhibiting, prompting the company to set up a booth this year to explore opportunities in the Chinese market. "We see the CIIE as a platform to start discussions with customers," he told Xinhua, adding that the company had already received a number of inquiries. TURNING MARKET ACCESS INTO SHARED OPPORTUNITIES For developing economies, access to a large market is only the starting point. Exporters also need to find buyers, understand consumer preferences and navigate market requirements, challenges that can be particularly difficult for smaller businesses. The Kenyan national pavilion is showcasing products from local exporters at this year's CIIE, as the East African country seeks to expand its presence in the Chinese market. Dennis Mwirigi, chairman of the Kenya Export Promotion and Branding Agency, welcomed China's zero-tariff treatment, which was expanded on May 1 to cover all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties, saying the policy would help boost Kenyan exports. "The increased market uptake is certainly going to create employment," he added, noting that growing demand for Kenyan agricultural products could generate jobs in farming, processing, transportation and cold-chain logistics. Latin American exhibitors are also seeking to turn opportunities at the CIIE into concrete business ties. El Salvador, participating in the CIIE for the fifth time, has brought 12 entrepreneurs to Shanghai to promote products including coffee, rum, shrimp sausages and handicrafts. Alejandro Rivas, a specialist at El Salvador's foreign ministry, said at least three of the entrepreneurs had already found Chinese importers through business exchanges during the expo. He also cited earlier sales of Salvadoran specialty coffee and rum worth more than 50,000 U.S. dollars, highlighting the potential for the Central American country's products in the Chinese market. For Nicaragua, the opportunities extend beyond finding buyers for its products. At its national pavilion, visitors can sample Nicaraguan products and learn about its export offerings. Alma Hernandez Altamirano, a representative of Nicaragua's export and investment promotion authorities, said participating businesses had established contacts during the first two days of the expo for follow-up meetings and potential negotiations. Nicaragua is also looking to China for agricultural processing machinery. According to Hernandez Altamirano, such equipment could help Nicaraguan producers increase output and lower costs while maintaining product quality, making their exports more competitive. FROM TRADE TO DEEPER COOPERATION For many overseas exhibitors, the CIIE is more than a six-day event. The connections established at the expo can develop into lasting business relationships, while continued engagement with the Chinese market can open up new areas of cooperation. Attending the CIIE for the third time, Ethiopia's MSA Business Group, an exporter of agricultural products, has developed lasting business relationships through the expo. Mershaye Kurabachew, the group's export director, said she first met one of her regular Chinese sesame buyers at the CIIE and reunited with the buyer at this year's event. Kurabachew also met potential new buyers this year, some of whom said they planned to visit the company in Ethiopia in December for further discussions. New Zealand company Hauora New Zealand has also witnessed how continued participation can help broaden business networks. Since attending the inaugural CIIE in 2018, it has seen its business connections expand beyond traditional importers and distributors to include e-commerce retailers, smaller import firms and group-buying businesses. Barbara Zhang, the company's general manager, said Chinese consumers have progressed from sampling products to placing online orders and making repeat purchases. "I see it as a very positive, self-reinforcing cycle," she said. Swedish industrial group Alfa Laval, participating in the CIIE for the sixth time, is showcasing technologies for efficient data center cooling and industrial waste heat recovery. Belinda Lau, president of the Energy Division at Alfa Laval China, said the exhibits respond to growing demand in China for advanced thermal management solutions. She noted that China is also one of the company's key global manufacturing bases, supplying both domestic and overseas markets. Lau said China's increasing focus on innovation and decarbonization is creating new opportunities for product development. "We can find new demands for new products so that we know what to develop," she said. (Video reporters: Liang Wanshan, Qiu Jingyi, Di Chun, Hong Jing; Video editors: Liang Wanshan, Zhu Cong, Zheng Xin, Hui Peipei)

item.title: Xi congratulates Iotova on election as Bulgarian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended congratulations to Iliana Iotova on her election as president of Bulgaria. In a message on Friday, Xi noted that Bulgaria was the second country in the world to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China, and that mutual respect, equality, and mutual benefit and win-win results have been hallmarks of the bilateral relations. In recent years, the two countries have been steadily advancing exchanges and cooperation at all levels and across all fields, while their strategic partnership has continued to deepen, said Xi. Xi also said that he attaches great importance to the development of the China-Bulgaria ties. He pledged to work with Iotova to guide the two countries as they march together along their respective paths to development and revitalization, build an even more positive, practical and dynamic bilateral relationship, and thereby bring greater benefits to the two peoples. ■

item.title: How Xi steers China's green transformation and global climate action
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- In 2026, the intensifying fallout of global climate change -- manifesting in catastrophic flooding, rampant wildfires, and record heatwaves -- reaffirms the imperative for immediate, coordinated global action. With global climate tipping points looming, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), set to kick off on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, will offer a new opportunity for the international community to renew momentum for more effective global climate cooperation. Under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China has over the years stayed committed to advancing ecological protection and green transition domestically, and promoting international climate cooperation, making major global contributions to the world's fight against what many regard as an existential threat to humanity. "LIKE WE PROTECT OUR EYES" "We should protect the environment like we protect our eyes." This evocative principle -- voiced on various occasions by Xi -- frames ecological conservation not merely as a policy choice, but as a vital imperative drawn directly from his own experiences. "Over four decades ago, I lived and worked for many years in a small village on the Loess Plateau in western China," Xi recalled in reply to a letter from student representatives of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate in 2020. Back then, the ecology and environment there was seriously damaged due to over-development, and the local people were trapped in poverty as a result. That experience has taught him that man and nature are a community of life and that the damage done to nature will ultimately hurt humanity. An avid reader of Chinese classics, Xi has also been deeply influenced by the traditional Chinese philosophy that views man as an integral part of nature. "All beings flourish when they live in harmony and receive nourishment from nature," he has said. This conviction underpins the signature environmental doctrine that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets," which Xi first introduced in 2005 while serving as Party chief of east China's Zhejiang Province. Upon becoming General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee in 2012, Xi made ecological conservation a national priority. For Xi, ecological conservation requires not only a profound shift in development philosophy, but also robust institutional safeguards. As he has put it, "Eco-environmental protection relies on laws and regulations." At his direction, environmental performance has become a key criterion for evaluating officials, while environmental inspections have reinforced local governments' accountability for fulfilling their environmental responsibilities. Together, these measures have helped steer China's economic growth toward a more resource-efficient and sustainable path. Since 2012, China has sustained a 6 percent average annual economic growth rate while capping an average energy consumption increase to just 3.3 percent. This structural decoupling yielded a 26.1 percent cumulative decline in energy intensity, marking one of the steepest efficiency gains globally. Xi has also led by example in promoting environmental protection and green development. Since becoming China's top leader, he has personally participated in tree-planting activities in Beijing for 14 consecutive years. Forests have the capacity to conserve water, bring in economic benefits, and boost grain production, and now serve well as a carbon sink, he has noted. Today, China has expanded its forest coverage to over 25 percent of its land area, planting trees across an area roughly 1.7 times the size of California since 2012. The annual carbon-sink capacity of China's forests and grassland has exceeded 1.2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents. Fuad Gani, vice director of the Graduate School of Sustainable Development at the University of Indonesia, said that China's ecological conservation philosophy stands out for its ability to translate environmental goals into long-term policies and governance frameworks. "It is one of China's most valuable contributions to advancing green transformation on the global stage," he said. "SOMETHING WE MUST DO OURSELVES" Balancing economic growth with green development remains a challenge for economies worldwide, especially emerging markets seeking to meet development needs while pursuing environmental sustainability. In Xi's view, economic growth and the green transition are not opposing forces, but complementary goals. This philosophy is captured in his defining doctrine -- "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." Achieving China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, Xi has stressed, "is not something that others ask us to do, but something we must do ourselves." Under his leadership, China has effectively aligned emissions reduction with technological innovation, industrial upgrading and energy security, turning the green transition into an increasingly important driver of high-quality development. As early as 2014, when conventional gasoline-powered vehicles still dominated China's roads, Xi recognized the enormous potential of new energy vehicles (NEVs). During an inspection tour of SAIC Motor, a major Chinese carmaker, Xi depicted developing NEVs as the only way for China to move from a major automobile country to an automobile powerhouse. In the following decade, the president has demonstrated consistent support for electric cars, visiting automotive companies, touring laboratories, and showing great interest in trying new home-developed models. China's NEV industry has since grown rapidly, emerging as a flagship of the country's technology-intensive manufacturing sector. Beyond the NEV sector, China has also built the world's largest and most comprehensive clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries emerging as an important engine of economic growth. The growing exports of the "new three" -- photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles -- are a testament to China's successful shift toward innovation-driven manufacturing. Beyond its own borders, China is now channeling this green innovation momentum into regional cooperation. China will continue to work with fellow Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) countries to increase the installed capacity of photovoltaic and wind power each by 10 million kilowatts, and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, said Xi at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO this September. China's exports of solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries this year will help the world to avoid 450 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to a recent analysis by the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The development exemplifies China's strategic push to cultivate "new quality productive forces" -- a policy concept first articulated by Xi in 2023 to drive high-tech innovation and sustainable economic modernization. "Green development," as Xi once put it, "is the defining feature of high-quality development, and new quality productive forces are green in nature." China has turned the challenges of addressing climate change into opportunities for technological innovation, industrial upgrading and high-quality economic development, said Wang Lei, a professor at the School of Government of Beijing Normal University. "Guided by the goals of reducing carbon emissions and strengthening climate resilience, the country has leveraged policy guidance, market incentives and open innovation to drive the transformation of energy, industry, transportation and construction," he added. "EXTREME RESOLUTIONS" Deeply committed to joining world nations to build a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi has repeatedly called on the international community to strengthen cooperation in addressing climate change and actively advanced the building of a fair and equitable global climate governance system for win-win cooperation. "Supreme resources spring from extreme resolutions," Xi said, invoking a perceptive line from French writer Victor Hugo's Les Miserables during his address to the historic 2015 Paris climate change conference. During the summit, Xi put forward important ideas and proposals and worked actively to build consensus among parties, making an indispensable contribution to the eventual adoption of the Paris Agreement. At a special ceremony on Sept. 3, 2016, Xi solemnly handed over China's instrument of joining the Paris Agreement to then UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. "Had not been President Xi Jinping's initiative, we would not have the Paris Agreement on climate change even now," Ban said in a 2021 interview with Xinhua. In response to the grave challenge of climate change, China has taken on its international responsibilities with what Xi described as "extreme resolutions." At a virtual UN gathering in 2020, Xi announced that China would strive to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. In 2021, he pledged that China would not build new coal-fired power projects abroad. In recent years, some developed countries, particularly those in the West, have backtracked on their climate commitments, undermining global climate governance. Against this backdrop, Xi announced China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions in 2025, including a commitment to reduce economy-wide net greenhouse gas emissions by 7-10 percent from peak levels and to raise the share of non-fossil fuels in total energy consumption to more than 30 percent by 2035. For the first time, China committed to absolute emissions reduction targets covering all economic sectors and all greenhouse gases, providing much-needed certainty and stability for global climate governance. Xi has also emphasized the need to uphold fairness and equity and fully respect developing countries' right to development as the world pursues a green transition. "The transition should serve to narrow rather than widen the North-South gap," he said, urging developed countries to take the lead in fulfilling emissions reduction obligations and provide more financial and technological support to developing countries. Under Xi's leadership, China has been striving to strengthen South-South cooperation on climate change. Xi has proposed the establishment of the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition and advocated building a green BRICS partnership. Through these target-driven initiatives, China seeks to deepen cooperation in clean energy, green technology and green industrial development, while helping developing countries strengthen their capacity to address climate change. "The Earth is our one and only home," Xi has said. "To scale up efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development bears on the future of humanity."■

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026.
